title.en: Physics timeline lifecycle and render interpolation

summary: Coordinate a fixed-step solver, variable-rate Three.js presentation and authored animation with one model-time lifecycle across run, pause, resume, reset and visibility changes.
objective: Display interpolated poses without feeding them into physics; pausing and hidden-tab time add no solver steps, resume causes no catch-up burst, and reset restores the complete initial snapshot and timing state.
applies_when: A fixed-step simulation is rendered at an independent display cadence.
Pause, reset, visibility changes or authored clip layers can otherwise leave stale accumulator, velocity or transform state.
intent_signals: pause physics without a catch-up jump
example_prompts: Run Rapier at fixed dt while Three.js interpolates display poses and pause excludes hidden-tab time.
Make reset restore bodies, velocities, sleeping flags, accumulator, animation time and ownership mode.
negative_signals: Advancing physics once per render callback with an arbitrary frame delta.
Resetting mesh positions while leaving solver velocities, contacts or accumulator intact.
not_for: A pure glTF clip with no numerical solver.
Claiming deterministic replay across engines, devices or floating-point builds without evidence.

principles: The existing fixed-step adapter owns accumulator and interpolation arithmetic. This motion profile owns lifecycle transitions: one model clock, one solver state, and a presentation pose derived read-only from completed states.

Pause is a model transition, not a small timestep: stop accumulation and integration, preserve the completed solver state and define whether authored visual layers freeze. Resume resets the wall-clock baseline so paused or hidden duration is excluded.

Reset is atomic across body poses, velocities, forces/impulses owned by the app, sleep/enabled/type flags, joints or controller state, previous/current presentation snapshots, accumulator, dropped-time counters, mixer time and ownership mode.
implementation: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop as the display callback. Convert its timestamp to finite nonnegative elapsed time, clamp according to the linked fixed-step policy, and never use display cadence itself as solver dt.

Before each solver step preserve the last completed state; after stepping capture the new state. Render an interpolation of those snapshots only. Solver-to-mesh synchronization occurs after all steps and before render, and never writes the blended mesh pose back.

On pause or visibility suspension, mark the clock baseline invalid and perform no integration. On resume initialize the baseline from the first callback. On reset stop conflicting mixers/controllers, restore one immutable initial snapshot, set previous=current, clear the accumulator/counters and render once.
observable_checks: With identical initial solver configuration and the same step-indexed input sequence, two display cadences produce matching completed-step state at equal model time within declared tolerance, provided neither run clamps or drops model time; wall-clock event ordering is outside this comparison.
A pause longer than the catch-up budget yields zero resume catch-up steps and no velocity or pose jump. Single-step while paused advances exactly one dt if offered.

After disturbance, reset immediately restores pose, velocity, body type, sleep policy, controller/mixer time, previous/current snapshots and zero accumulator; a second run repeats the same lifecycle sequence.

creative_affordances: Show previous/current ghosts, a model-time dial or dropped-time indicator when useful; these are optional inspection devices.
Slow motion may alter wall-time consumption while leaving the solver dt fixed and visibly reporting the time scale.
known_limits: A fixed timestep and careful lifecycle do not prove numerical convergence, deterministic cross-platform replay or collision completeness.
Browser visibility and XR scheduling need artifact-specific tests; Three.js loop documentation does not define application pause semantics.
Authored guidance only; no render loop, visibility transition, solver or reset test was run.

claims.statement: Rapier IntegrationParameters.dt is the time advanced by each physics update and defaults to 1/60 second; smaller steps generally improve accuracy, while larger steps amplify approximation error and can miss fast collisions.
claims.scope: Rapier JavaScript integration guidance; application accumulator, pause and reset policy is authored here and linked to the existing fixed-step adapter.

claims.statement: Three.js recommends WebGLRenderer.setAnimationLoop for the application render loop, while AnimationMixer.update advances authored animation by a supplied delta time and setTime moves it to an explicit time.
claims.scope: Current Three.js renderer and animation APIs; neither API defines a physics pause/reset contract.
